body:
## Summary

`expand_with_margins()`, `nest_with_margins()`, and `nest_by_with_margins()`
fail on a `dtplyr` input whenever a Margin dimension is `integer`, `double`,
`Date`, or `logical` and the margin label is a non-missing string. The same
call on the same data through the local `data.frame` backend succeeds.

`?expand_with_margins` says the verb "works with local data frames and `dtplyr`
steps", and *Display labels and grouping identity* says a non-missing label
converts an ordinary dimension to character. Neither happens here: the call
raises from data.table, naming nothing the caller wrote.

`summarize_with_margins()` is unaffected — its omitted dimension does not reach
the branch as a column of the input.

## Reproduction

```r
pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

df <- data.frame(i = c(1L, 1L, 2L), v = 1:3)

expand_with_margins(df, .grouping = rollup(i))                     # works
expand_with_margins(dtplyr::lazy_dt(df), .grouping = rollup(i)) |>
  collect()                                                        # fails
```

```
Warning in `[.data.table`(copy(`_DT1`), , `:=`(i = "Total")) :
  Coercing 'character' RHS to 'integer' to match the type of column 1 named 'i'
Warning: NAs introduced by coercion
Error in .set_ops_arg_check(x, y, all, block_list = !all) :
  Item 1 of x is 'character' but the corresponding item of y is 'integer'.
```

Measured over one dimension of each type, on `dtplyr::lazy_dt()`:

| Dimension type | `expand` | `nest` | `nest_by` | `summarize` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `integer` | fails | fails | fails | ok |
| `double` | fails | — | — | ok |
| `Date` | fails | — | — | ok |
| `logical` | fails | — | — | ok |
| `character` | ok | ok | ok | ok |
| `factor` | ok | ok | ok | ok |

The `double`, `Date`, and `logical` rows raise the same error with
`'numeric'`, `'Date'`, and `'logical'` in place of `'integer'`.
`.margin_label = NULL` and `.margin_label = NA_character_` are unaffected on
every type.

## Root cause

`label_margin_branch()` (`R/margin-label.R:383`) writes the label into an
omitted dimension as a scalar in `dplyr::mutate(.data, !!!values)`. dtplyr
renders a scalar overwrite as data.table `:=`, which coerces the RHS to the
column's *existing* type rather than replacing the column. The omitted branch
therefore keeps `integer` where the included branches carry `character`, and
`funion()` refuses the pair.

The factor arm at `R/margin-label.R:467-481` already carries the fix for its
own case, and its comment states the mechanism:

> dtplyr renders a scalar overwrite as data.table `:=`. On a multi-row factor
> column, data.table recycles it without replacing the column class [...] A
> full-size value replaces the column so factor restoration remains after the
> union.

The same is true of every other non-character type; only factors were given
`rep(!!label, dplyr::n())`.

## Fix direction

Widen the `dtplyr_factor_cols` arm to any column that is not already
`character` on a `dtplyr_step`, so the labelled value is written full-size
there too. `labelled_included` above it converts *included* columns with
`as.character()`; the omitted ones have no equivalent.

## What is unmeasured

- Whether any other backend renders a scalar overwrite the same way. The union
  adapter's SQL backends were not tested for this, since the label there is
  built inside the branch query rather than by a `mutate()` on a step.
- Whether a list-column or a `difftime` dimension behaves as the four types
  above.

title: dtplyr expand and nest fail on every non-character, non-factor dimension carrying a margin label
